source_caption:
Michael Fassbender committed fully to the vulnerability of Shame, working closely with director Steve McQueen to strip away dialogue and rely on physical performance and silence to portray addiction in a raw, unfiltered way.

Shame (2011), directed by Steve McQueen, starring Michael Fassbender, Carey Mulligan, James Badge Dale. A stark and intimate character study that explores loneliness, desire, and self-destruction in modern life with unflinching honesty.

source_details.title: Shame
source_details.synopsis: Shame is a 2011 British psychological drama film produced by Film4 and See-Saw Films, directed by Steve McQueen, and co-written by McQueen and Abi Morgan. It stars Michael Fassbender as a sex addicted New Yorker named Brandon, whose life starts to unravel when his younger sister (Carey Mulligan) shows up in his life. The film's explicit scenes reflecting the protagonist's sexual addiction resulted in a rating of NC-17 in the United States. Shame premiered at the 68th Venice International Film Festival, where it was selected for its main competition and where Fassbender won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor.
